title: Measuring Reward Hacking and Reasoning-Answer Decoupling Under Position-Confounded Optimization
abstract: arXiv:2608.15445v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When a reward is correct on every training example yet consistent with more than one goal, a model can acquire an unintended one, a failure known as goal misgeneralization. Endpoint accuracy on the training distribution cannot tell the two apart, because solving the task and exploiting a surface feature can satisfy the reward equally well. We treat this as a measurement problem: what does a benchmark score measure once a model has been optimized against a correct but confounded signal? We train language models with GRPO on multiple-choice math problems where the correct answer is always option A, then evaluate on an unseen test set with unbiased answer positions. Across Qwen2.5, Llama 3.x and Gemma-3 models, biased training often drives option-A rates above 0.90 in smaller models and collapses unbiased accuracy toward chance, so accuracy stops measuring math ability and instead measures an answer-position policy. translated_title: 测量位置混杂优化下的奖励黑客行为与推理-答案解耦
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.15445v1 公告类型：新 摘要：当奖励在每个训练样本上都是正确的，却与多个目标一致时，模型可能会习得一个非预期目标，这种失败被称为目标泛化错误。训练分布上的端点准确率无法区分这两者，因为解决任务和利用表面特征可以同样好地满足奖励。我们将此视为一个测量问题：一旦模型针对正确但混杂的信号进行优化，基准分数究竟在测量什么？我们使用GRPO在正确答案始终为选项A的多项选择数学问题上训练语言模型，然后在答案位置无偏的未见测试集上进行评估。在Qwen2.5、Llama 3.x和Gemma-3模型中，有偏训练常使较小模型的选项A比率超过0.90，并将无偏准确率降至随机水平，因此准确率不再衡量数学能力，而是衡量一种答案位置策略。我们进一步发现推理...
tldr: 本研究揭示了在位置混杂优化下，模型可能通过奖励黑客行为（如偏好选项A）而非真正推理来提升训练准确率，导致无偏测试性能崩溃，并首次系统量化了推理-答案解耦现象。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that under position-confounded optimization, models may exploit reward hacking (e.g., preferring option A) rather than genuine reasoning, collapsing unbiased accuracy, and systematically quantifies the reasoning-answer decoupling phenomenon.
